title: The Oath in the Peach Garden
text:
The Romance of the Three Kingdoms, the great fourteenth century Chinese novel attributed to Luo Guanzhong, opens in 184, as the Han dynasty totters and the Yellow Turban rebellion spreads.

In the county of Zhuo a notice goes up calling for volunteers to fight the rebels. Liu Bei, a poor man who sells straw sandals and mats but claims descent from the imperial house, reads it and sighs. Zhang Fei, a butcher and wine seller with a booming voice, scolds him for sighing instead of acting. In a tavern they meet Guan Yu, a tall, red-faced man with a long beard, on the run after killing a local bully.

The three find they share the same hopes. In the peach garden behind Zhang Fei's house, among the blossoms, they sacrifice a black ox and a white horse and swear brotherhood before Heaven and Earth. They vow to help each other and the people, and declare that though they were not born on the same day, they wish to die on the same day. Liu Bei becomes the eldest brother, Guan Yu the second, Zhang Fei the third.

The novel follows their loyalty through decades of war, until Liu Bei founds the kingdom of Shu. The historical record, Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms, does not mention any oath, but it does say that Liu Bei treated Guan Yu and Zhang Fei with the affection of brothers and that they followed him through every hardship.
lesson: A small group bound by clear, mutual commitment can hold together through long years of setbacks. Say out loud what you owe each other.
people: Liu Bei, Guan Yu, Zhang Fei
source: Luo Guanzhong, Romance of the Three Kingdoms, chapter 1; Chen Shou, Records of the Three Kingdoms (Sanguozhi), biography of Guan Yu
caveat: The oath is a literary invention of the novel; the history records only that the three were close as brothers.
